intro: Priya's been running some version of this deck since she joined, and the plan hasn't really changed: bounce whatever's in the way, get something unblockable through, and let Ninja of the Deep Hours do the rest. It's not a flashy deck. It just doesn't let the other player settle into whatever they were trying to do.

Get an evasive creature down early and protect it with bounce when you need to. Once the ninja's connecting, you're drawing extra cards most turns, and most games you're not doing anything spectacular — you're just quietly ahead by the time anyone notices.

howToPlay.heading: Mulligan guide
howToPlay.text: Keep any hand with two lands, an evasive one-or-two-drop, and either a bounce spell or a cantrip. Slither Blade into Ninja of the Deep Hours is the dream opening — don't be afraid to mulligan a hand that can't produce it by turn three.

howToPlay.heading: Early game
howToPlay.text: Deploy your unblockable threats on curve and hold Vapor Snag for anything that would trade with or block them. You're almost never the beatdown before turn four, so early on your only real job is keeping that one relevant creature connecting.

howToPlay.heading: Mid game
howToPlay.text: Once Ninja of the Deep Hours is online, every attack should be asking 'what does two extra cards let me do next turn.' Use Exclude to strip your opponent's best answer and Mulldrifter to refill after a trade. Deep Analysis with flashback means a slow hand is rarely a dead hand.

howToPlay.heading: Closing it out
howToPlay.text: You rarely need more than two or three unblocked attacks to draw enough cards to bury the opponent. Once you're ahead, start trading resources freely — falling behind on board is fine as long as you're still ahead on cards.

sideboardGuide.notes: You're on the draw against a deck that wants to race — buy time and let your card advantage take over from turn six onward.
Protect your evasive threats and hold up counter mana once you're ahead. They're the ones who need to catch up on cards, not you.
Annul answers everything they're doing for one mana. Prioritize their equipment and key artifact lands over their creatures.
Echoing Truth is a two-for-one against their mana dorks. Don't try to race — Fog buys the turn you need to stabilize.
